speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pseudogout is unlikely given the age; the clinical picture of an 18-month-old male with monoarticular knee swelling, no clear trauma, and a strong family history is highly suggestive of Hemophilia A or B (hemarthrosis), or potentially a genetic condition like Familial Mediterranean Fever or a crystal arthropathy such as CPPD (less common in infants). To confirm, I need to assess bleeding tendencies and joint fluid.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, PT/INR, PTT, and Joint_Aspiration (synovial fluid analysis).
